messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: rstan arguments
parts:
stan() has an argument called iter. It should be called n_iter. Also, the description in the help file is "A positive integer specifying how many iterations for all the chains (including warmup). The default is 2000." It should say "each chain" rather than "all the chains".

Also I think we should use n_warmup and n_thin rather than warmup and thin.

A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] rstan arguments
parts:
Nothing is stopping us from changing the names, but to me, iter, warmup, and thin make as much sense as n_iter, n_warmup, and n_thin. I think anyone who has done any MCMC before would expect there to be an positive integer argument for the iterations and the thinning interval. But warmup is more difficult because it is nonstandard. I could see an experienced MCMC user thinking that warmup might be binary or something but making the connection that n_warmup was supposed to be a positive integer.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c

On 8/31/12 10:55 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Friday, August 31, 2012 3:37:49 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> And that'll take us to version 1.1.0 already, because
> we'll be breaking backward compatibility in our
> very first patch.
>
>
> I would say there should be a general rule that changes which break previously working code should increment the major
> number. Also, as a general rule, we should write the general rules down.

Absolutely right. I even DID write those
rules down in the doc :-)

For me, changing the names now will be a medium
hassle for us.

-- we have to change code in R and C++ and in the
R that calls C++
-- we have to change the doc on the R and C++ side,
in the manual, on the web (actually, may not be
mentioned there explicitly), and in the manual
-- we have to release another version
-- we have to explain the change to users

It imposes a minor, but measurable negative impact
on the users having to update right out of the gate.
It's not huge, but it's not great for the trust you
need between users and developers.

And on top of all that, I like them better the way they
are, which is why I chose those names in the first place!

Having said all that, I'm not as concerned about
changing the command-line option names as I am changing
the model syntax.

- Bob
